slides.title: How a quantum dot emits
slides.subtitle: From a few-level solid to a measurable quantum optical source
slides.notes: We follow emission from confined carriers to detector statistics, keeping the quantum device, quantum dot, and quantum light claims separate. [Fox 2006] [Project's own treatment slides]

slides.title: What does ‘quantum’ mean here?

columns.heading: Quantum treatment of light
bullets: Quantised field, Fock states, and operators.
Normally ordered g² tests the output.

slides.notes: The owner's slides define a quantum device through carrier confinement and Coulomb blockade, not automatically through a quantum optical output. Field quantisation, Fock states, and normally ordered correlations are a separate claim. [Project's own treatment slides] [Loudon]
sources: Loudon, The Quantum Theory of Light

slides.title: Quantum treatment of the dot versus the light
slides.notes: A quantum treatment of the dot follows internal states and phonons. A quantum treatment of light follows field modes and output correlations. The repository is Level 2: rate and cascade identities, not a field-quantised density matrix. [Project's own treatment slides] [Gardiner 1985]

slides.title: What a single-photon source must meet
slides.notes: The program conditions are electrical injection, an InP/GaAsP epitaxial dot, integrated SiN collection, and a 300 K ambition staged through 77–120 K. Purity, brightness, indistinguishability, and timing are independent acceptance gates. [Project's own treatment slides] [Reischle 2008]

slides.title: Light–matter coupling
bullets: Interband dcv contains the Bloch matrix element.
Kane energy EP packages band-edge coupling.

equations.latex: H_{int}=-\mathbf d\cdot\mathbf E,\quad d_{cv}=\langle u_c|e\mathbf r|u_v\rangle
equations.caption: d is dipole, E field, and uc, uv periodic Bloch functions.

slides.notes: The dipole Hamiltonian connects the confined interband transition to the optical field. Envelope overlap, the Kane matrix element, strain, and HH/LH mixing determine strength and polarisation. [Chuang] [Yu and Cardona]
sources: Yu and Cardona, Fundamentals of Semiconductors

slides.title: From golden rule to spontaneous emission
bullets: A dot lifetime is commonly in the 1 ns class.

equations.caption: n, ω, d, ε0, ħ, c are index, frequency, dipole, vacuum permittivity, reduced Planck constant, and light speed.
f is oscillator strength; m0 and e are free-electron mass and charge.

slides.notes: Fermi's golden rule sums dipole-coupled vacuum modes and gives the cubic-frequency spontaneous rate. Oscillator strength is a dimensionless reporting form. The repository takes radiative rates as model inputs. [Fox 2006] [Michler 2017]

slides.title: Two-level atom versus quantum dot

columns.heading: Jaynes–Cummings
bullets: H contains one emitter and one cavity mode.

slides.notes: The two-level approximation isolates one dipole, while a dot adds XX, charge, spin, and phonon structure. The Jaynes–Cummings model distinguishes irreversible Purcell enhancement from strong-coupling exchange. [Purcell 1946] [Michler 2017]

slides.title: Exciton, biexciton, and trion ladder
bullets: ΔXX controls XX leakage through an X filter.

equations.caption: EX is exciton energy and Ebind,XX biexciton binding energy.

slides.notes: The biexciton binding shift separates XX and X lines. That same cascade enables pair protocols and creates a multiphoton impurity when XX leaks through an X filter. [Bimberg 1999] [Michler 2017]

slides.title: Fine structure and entangled photon pairs
bullets: Near-degenerate paths can yield entangled pairs.
Pair fidelity and single-photon purity differ.
slides.notes: Fine-structure splitting controls the phase between biexciton decay paths. Small splitting supports polarisation entanglement; this is distinct from the HBT purity objective. [Michler 2017] [Qian et al. 2025]

slides.title: Cascade rate equations
bullets: Pump r loads X and XX.
γ terms radiate; k terms escape.
generator and steady_state implement this ladder.

equations.caption: NXX is biexciton population; r pump; γXX radiative rate; kXX escape.
NX and N0 are exciton and empty populations.

slides.notes: fsim_core/cw_g2.py uses the ordered states 0, X, XX. generator builds the three-state Markov matrix and steady_state returns its stationary populations. It is a population model with no optical coherences, appropriate for incoherent electrical pumping. [fsim_core/cw_g2.py]

slides.title: Photon statistics: what HBT measures
bullets: A single emitter recovers after a jump.
slides.notes: The HBT correlation compares conditional and unconditional detection rates. The classical Cauchy–Schwarz bound is one at zero delay; a single emitter dips below one because it cannot immediately re-emit after a jump. Background and detector response reshape the observed dip. [Fox 2006] [Loudon]
sources: Loudon, The Quantum Theory of Light

slides.title: Background turns a perfect dip upward
bullets: The background is independent and Poissonian.

equations.caption: s and b are signal and background means; ρ is signal fraction.

slides.notes: Expanding the second moment of signal plus independent Poisson background gives the exact mixture law. Even a perfect signal dip is lifted toward one as background increases. [Reischle 2008] [fsim_core/device.py]

slides.title: Cap-2 Poisson loading

equations.caption: μ is mean loading; ε=tXX/tX is leakage.

slides.notes: For Poisson loading capped at two excitons, the repository derives the pulsed peak-area ratio from P0, P1, P2 and filter leakage epsilon. Weak loading recovers the F1 identity; stronger loading adds a finite-pulse multiphoton penalty. [fsim_core/loading.py] [Hanschke 2018]
sources: Hanschke et al., npj Quantum Information 4, 43 (2018)

slides.title: CW g² and quantum regression
bullets: The propagator follows a detected jump.
cw_report returns intrinsic, background, and IRF curves.
CW and pulsed g² are different observables.

figure.caption: cw_report curves for 80 K and 300 K cards.

slides.notes: cw_g2.py applies the regression idea to the classical three-state generator: after X detection the dot is empty, after XX detection it is in X. The low-pump limit is epsilon times pump ratio times retention ratio. This is a rate-equation regression, not a fully quantised field calculation. [Gardiner 1985] [fsim_core/cw_g2.py]

slides.title: Detector response is part of the measurement
bullets: erfcx gives a stable closed form.
A 5 ps dip is diluted by 100 ps IRF.

equations.caption: A is dip depth, τd recovery time, σ Gaussian IRF width.

slides.notes: The detector response convolves the intrinsic correlation. cw_g2.py provides Gaussian and exponential IRF forms and a stable erfcx expression. When the response is much slower than the recovery dip, the raw zero-delay value approaches one. [fsim_core/cw_g2.py] [Reischle 2008]

slides.title: Phonons I: sidebands and the independent-boson model
bullets: Acoustic phonons couple to charge density.
A ZPL sits on a broad sideband.
Temperature transfers weight to the sideband.

equations.caption: C is dipole coherence; Z is ZPL fraction; S is Huang–Rhys factor.

slides.notes: qd_gf.py implements the acoustic deformation-potential independent-boson lineshape, including ZPL and sideband transmission. It does not yet include piezoelectric or microscopic LO coupling, nor driven polaron renormalisation. [Krummheuer 2002] [fsim_core/qd_gf.py]

slides.title: Phonons II: linewidth grows with temperature
bullets: The coded 300 K envelope is 6–20 meV.

equations.caption: Γ0 residual width, a acoustic slope, b LO coupling, ELO LO energy.

slides.notes: The phenomenological linewidth model separates acoustic and activated optical-phonon contributions. At 300 K the repository envelope ranges from 6 to 20 meV, a design class rather than a target-dot measurement. [Matsuda 2001] [Chatzarakis 2023] [fsim_core/linewidth.py]

slides.title: Band-gap and line shift with temperature
bullets: Varshni shift moves X and XX.
InP and GaAs do not walk identically.
A filter must track the selected line.

equations.caption: E0 is zero-temperature gap; α and β are Varshni parameters.

slides.notes: Temperature shifts the dot transition relative to barriers and filters. Material-dependent Varshni coefficients make filter tracking a device requirement, because tX and tXX change together. [Vurgaftman 2001] [Yu and Cardona]

slides.title: Spectral overlap sets biexciton leakage
bullets: Lorentzian lines pass through one window.
Larger ΔXX helps; larger Γ hurts.

figure.caption: ε versus Γ for ΔXX=4, 6, 8 meV.

slides.notes: spectral.epsilon computes the ratio of XX and X transmissions through the same acceptance function. At the worked point DeltaXX=6 meV, GammaX=GammaXX=12 meV, and window 12 meV, the repository returns epsilon 0.7048327647. [fsim_core/spectral.py] [Chatzarakis 2023]

slides.title: Thermal escape and retention
bullets: Ea follows confinement and escape paths.

equations.caption: S retention; Ea,Eb activations; a,b prefactors.

slides.notes: dot_levels.retention_params derives two Arrhenius escape channels from the confinement model. The coded InP/GaAsP preset returns Ea=83.7949596801 meV under its pair-half convention; this is an assumption-class proxy, not Measurement 1. Exponential thermal loss can dominate brightness. [Chatzarakis 2023] [Bommer 2011] [fsim_core/dot_levels.py]

slides.title: Indistinguishability: the other quantum metric
bullets: Phonons and charge noise raise γ*.
Low g² does not guarantee HOM visibility.
slides.notes: Indistinguishability depends on optical coherence, not only population statistics. The repository does not compute the photon density matrix or HOM visibility; this is an explicit Level-3 gap from the owner's slides. [Iles-Smith 2017] [Project's own treatment slides]

slides.title: Putting the model together: the 300 K landscape
bullets: Sweep axes are Γ(300 K) and ΔXX.
No reviewed electrical III–V row is below 0.5.
slides.notes: The landscape is a design sensitivity map, not evidence. It shows how linewidth and biexciton separation jointly control leakage. The owner's brief gates every 300 K number on Measurement 1 of Gamma(T) and DeltaXX for the actual InP/GaAsP dot. The reviewed optical Laferriere result reaches 0.57 at 300 K; the electrical arsenide/phosphide target remains open. [Chatzarakis 2023] [Laferriere 2023]

slides.title: Experimental status at the conditions
slides.subtitle: Restated from the project's own treatment slides
bullets: Electrical cryogenic SPS, optical warm SPS, and room-temperature edge-emitting QD lasers are distinct evidence classes.
No reviewed row combines electrical, 300 K, InP/GaAsP, edge collection, and g²<0.5.
slides.notes: Deshpande supplies a room-temperature electrical nitride anchor; Laferriere supplies an optical warm InAsP/InP anchor; Chatzarakis supplies warm-dot X/XX context. None is the complete target platform. [Project's own treatment slides]

slides.title: How our model integrates this
slides.notes: The repository maps materials and confinement into thermal optical response, then maps transmission, loading, background, and rate propagation into observables. It is a validated Level-2 semiclassical stack; quantised field modes and HOM are not implemented. [Project's own treatment slides] [fsim_core modules]

slides.title: What is left
bullets: Measure Γ(T) and ΔXX to 300 K on one electrical dot.
Demonstrate confinement and edge collection together.
Calibrate background, IRF, filter, and pulsing.
Add HOM visibility and electrical-pulsing data.
Treat the sweep as design guidance, not evidence.
slides.notes: The remaining work is Measurement 1, transport-to-emitter coupling, driven phonon dynamics, field-quantised regression, and an experimental acceptance chain including HOM. The project brief records these as open rather than silently extrapolating. [Kantner 2017] [Project's own treatment slides]

slides.title: Section summary
slides.subtitle: Emission is a chain: ladder → coupling → statistics → temperature limits
bullets: Discrete states do not alone certify quantum light.
Purity combines loading, leakage, background, and IRF.
Temperature couples linewidth, escape, and filter alignment.
Next: electrical injection and edge-emitting device physics.
slides.notes: We connected the dipole and golden rule to the exciton ladder, rate equations, HBT statistics, finite loading, background, detector response, phonons, linewidth, spectral overlap, and retention. The central distinction from the owner's slides remains: a quantum device, quantum dot treatment, and quantum light treatment are different claims. [Fox 2006] [Project's own treatment slides]
